name: Mechanical Engineering
department: School of Technology (curriculum issued under the old name PDPU)
handbook: Course Structure w.e.f. Academic Year 2016-17 (OLD curriculum, see note)
notes: IMPORTANT: The only Mechanical file you sent is the OLD 2016-17 curriculum (issued when PDEU was still PDPU). It does not match the 2024+ structure that every other branch follows, so treat this section as outdated. The current Mechanical handbook is not among the files.
This file is a scanned/odd-encoded PDF, so its text was read with OCR. Read the topics as accurate in substance, but small spelling slips from OCR are possible.
The 2016 file does not give course categories. Categories (BSC/ESC/PC/HSC) were assigned here by subject type so core vs not-core could be marked.

Department Elective III & IV options (Sem VII): Experimental Stress Analysis, Science and Technology of Welding, CFD and Heat Transfer, Rapid Product Development, Planning of Facilities and Materials Handling Systems, Vibration Engineering Design, Design for Manufacturing, Fuels Combustion and Pollution, Automotive Design, Lubrication, Micro- & Nano-Manufacturing, Cryogenics. Their syllabi are not in the file.

Department Elective V options (Sem VIII): ML Applications in Design and Manufacturing, Heat Exchangers Design, Automobile Engineering, Solar Photovoltaic Fundamentals, Procurement and Material Management, Flexible Manufacturing Systems, Advances in Measurement Techniques.

Semester VIII has two routes: Major in-house project (CAM + Thermal Engineering & Power Plant + Project Management/Elective V + 12-credit project) OR Comprehensive project (Thermal Engineering & Power Plant + Project Management/Elective V + 16-credit project + seminar).

units.title: Unit 1
topics: The moral question is a subjective and relative question
This introductory unit deals with the problem of managing the personal within the collective definitions of moral

units.title: Unit 2
topics: Is what ismorally good commanded by God because it is morally good, or is it morally good because it is commanded by God?” Ever since Plato’s original discussion
this question has presented a problem for some theists
though others have thought it a false dilemma, and it continues to be an object of theological and philosophical discussion today

units.title: Unit 3
topics: Utilitarianism is defined as the science of utility
Most modern amenities and engineering products are based on a utilitarian rational
the central problem with this approach to ethical life is that it fails to take into considerations of Justice
racism was justified as a utilitarian principle
Individualism questions the greatest benefit to greatest number theory
This unit will open up the thinking of students to various ways in which they can imagine their role in society as professionals
A question they should ask of themselves is “Do | want to be the best
best engineer/student/individual or do | want to be the best good engineer/student/individual?”

units.title: Unit 4
topics: At the end of this essential reading which prescribes a duty bound system of ethics
students are likely to ponder over the means/end problem
Kantian ethics is deeply opposed to a consequentialist ethics
In some ways all rationale is consequentialist in nature

units.title: Unit 5
topics: This unit lays bare the Rawlsian difference between the “Good thing” and the “Right thing
Sandel in his Harvard lectures uses contemporary issues to drive home the point that making ethical choices can never be an individual choice
His book and video lectures should pave way for engaging discussions in the class

units.title: Unit 6
topics: This movie focused unit will raise an important debate surrounding the question of universal logic
The close relation between mathematics and philosophy is explored in the backdrop of the troubling question: Is there an absolute truth?

units.title: Unit 7
topics: This is a case study focused lecture.Two popular ethical questions involving the engineering community in Indian society are the use of nuclear energy and construction of large scale dams
Both of these technologies and utilitarian in nature but have been met with widespread conflict
a debate on public good” can be initiated
